headlines.title: Why Netflix Stock Is At A One-Year Low
headlines.summary: Our Nov 16 piece, Can Netflix Stock Fall 50%, found that Netflix (NFLX) has fallen 50% or more from high to low in three of the 15 market shocks it has traded through. That is the crash question. The next question is the one owners live with every day: what is the real risk now, with no shock in sight.

headlines.title: NFLX Stock Edges Higher Overnight: Evercore Swaps Netflix For Spotify On Top Picks List
headlines.summary: Evercore ISI noted that Spotify’s stock had recently rallied 30%, making it a better pick than Netflix, which is currently trading within 10% of its three-year lows.

headlines.title: Netflix Stock Now Trades at a 70% Discount to Its Peak Valuation, and One Number Is to Blame
headlines.summary: Market sentiment has taken a negative turn for a business investors considered a perennial winner.

headlines.title: Netflix Lowers 2026 Ad Revenue Forecast: Time to Hold the Stock?
headlines.summary: NFLX cuts its 2026 ad revenue forecast to $2.7B, but strong margins, cash flow and a packed content slate support holding the stock despite valuation risks.

description: Netflix, Inc. provides entertainment services worldwide. The company offers television (TV) series, documentaries, feature films, games, and live programming across various genres and languages. It also provides members the ability to receive streaming content through a host of internet-connected devices, including TVs, digital video players, TV set-top boxes, and mobile devices. Netflix, Inc. was incorporated in 1997 and is headquartered in Los Gatos, California.
